{{minitoc}}
==English==

===Etymology 1===
{{dercat|en|qfa-sub|fro|frk|gem-pro}}
Early Modern English (c. 1500) slang term meaning "beggar's child".<ref>{{R:OED Online|id=1812251052}}</ref> Possibly from {{der|en|sco|bratchet|t=bitch, hound}}, in which case it would be a {{dbt|en|brachet|nocap=1}}. Another possibility is that it was originally a dialectal word, from northern and western England and the [[Midlands]], for a "makeshift or ragged garment," from {{der|en|ang|bratt|t=cloak}}, which is from a {{der|en|cel|-}} source ({{der|en|sga|-}} {{m|ga|brat|t=cloak, cloth}}).

In the sense "characteristic of a confident and assertive woman", {{coinage|en|Charli XCX|nat=English|occ=singer and songwriter|nocap=1}} in her 2024 album ''{{w|Brat (album)|Brat}}'',<ref>{{R:Dictionary.com|url=https://www.dictionary.com/e/pop-culture/brat/}}</ref> though occasional earlier uses of the word with a "reclaimed" or [[ironic]], positive [[connotation]] existed, including in {{w|LGBTQ slang}} for people of certain [[femme]] or feminine-leaning personalities.

* {{enPR|brăt}}, {{IPA|en|/bɹæt/}}
* {{audio|en|en-au-brat.ogg|a=AU}}
* {{rhymes|en|æt|s=1}}
* {{hyph|en|brat}}
* {{hmp|en|Bratt}}

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|slang|usually|negative connotation}} A [[human]] [[child]].
#: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:child}}
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2 March 2012|author=Dan Shive|title=El Goonish Shive|section=Comic for Friday, Mar 2, 2012|sectionurl=https://www.egscomics.com/comic/2012-03-02|format=webcomic|text="So... ''you'' want to have kids someday?"  "''Uh...'' well, yes.  I always figured I'd have a couple '''brats''' of my own someday..."  "That's still doable, you know."  "I know, but the process is a lot more complicated and less intimate, and --"}}
## {{lb|en|pejorative}} A [[child]] who is regarded as [[mischievous]], [[unruly]], [[spoil]]ed, or [[selfish]].
##: {{co|en|a spoiled '''brat'''}}
##: {{ux|en|Get that little '''brat''' away from me!}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1850|author=w:Thomas Keightley|title=The Fairy Mythology|location=London|publisher=H.G. Bohn|page=522|passage=“But it was far otherwise wid the remainin' one, which was the ouldest; he was the most miserable, ugly, ill-conditioned '''brat''' that ivir God put life into: he was so ill thriven, that he was nivir able to stand alone or to lave his cradle; he had long, shaggy, matted, curly hair, as black as the sut; his face was uv a greenish yollow colour[.]”}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1886|translator=H.L. Br&aelig;kstad|author=w:Peter Christen Asbjørnsen|title=Folk and Fairy Tales|page=297|passage=He would never speak a word, - only eat and cry, and she hadn't the heart to strike it or illtreat the youngster either; but somebody taught her a charm to make him speak, and then she found out what kind of a '''brat''' he really was.}}
## {{lb|en|uncountable|neologism}} The qualities possessed by a [[confident#Adjective|confident]] and [[assertive#Adjective|assertive]] [[woman#Noun|woman]].
##* {{RQ:WaPo|author=Lauren Bulbin|author2=Annaliese Nurnberg|title=The best brat styles of DNC|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/style/2024/08/23/dnc-brat-fashion-celebrities-photos/|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/AZbm4|archivedate=23 August 2024|date=23 August 2024|passage=Here are the people and the styles at the DNC that embodied the '''brat''' ethos.}}
##* {{RQ:New Yorker|author=w:Lena Dunham|title=A Guide to Brat Summer|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240827015238/https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2024/09/02/a-guide-to-brat-summer|date=26 August 2024|passage='''Brat''' is being lazy until 10 P.M., at which point you construct a château using discarded scraps of pleather, finish it by morning, and immediately win the Pritzker Architecture Prize.}}
##* {{quote-web|en|author=Brooke LaMantia|title=Naomi Osaka Is Having a Brat U.S. Open|site=[[w:The Cut (website)|The Cut]]|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240828025235/https://www.thecut.com/article/naomi-osaka-is-having-a-brat-u-s-open.html|date=27 August 2024|passage=My favorite touch is how each of her Nike shoes has its own little bow, which is just the perfect amount of '''brat'''.}}
## {{lb|en|slang}} A [[child]] (at any age) of an active member of the [[military]] or the [[diplomatic service]].
##: {{co|en|an army '''brat'''}}
##* {{quote-journal|en|date=1941-06-05|author=Gerry Dick|title=They Practiced Art of War, Then They Studied It|newspaper=Hope Star|location=Hope, Arkansas|page=5|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/hope-star-1941-06-05/page/n4/mode/1up?q=brat|passage=Lt. Gen. John L. DeWitt, Commander of the Fourth Army, was an army “'''brat''',” which means his father was an army officer. But he went into the army from Princeton, not from West Point.}}
## {{senseid|en|unruly submissive}} {{lb|en|BDSM}} A [[submissive]] partner who is [[disobedient]] and [[unruly]].
# {{lb|en|by extension|pejorative}} An [[immature]], [[spoil]]ed and/or [[selfish]] person.
# A [[turbot]] or [[flatfish]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1843|author={{w|Thomas Wilson (poet)|Thomas Wilson}}|title=The Movement|chapter=|edition=|url=[http://books.google.com/books?id=nvkDAAAAQAAJ&pg=PA127 The Pitman's Pay: And Other Poems]|passage=For the ''crabby'' awd dealers in ''ling'', ''cod'', and '''''brats''''' / And the ''vurgins'' that tempt us wi' nice ''maiden skyet''...}}
# {{senseid|en|cloak}}{{lb|en|historic}} A rough [[cloak]] or ragged [[garment]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1961 |title=Everyday costume in Britain: from the earliest times to 1900  |author=Audrey I. Barfoot  |page=80 |ISBN= |passage=The chief's daughter wears a '''brat''' and léine girdled with a criss. }}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2005 |title=Medieval Ireland: An Encyclopedia  |author=Seán Duffy  |page=156 |ISBN=1135948240 |passage=The prevailing style of dress in the early medieval period comprised a léine (tunic) worn under a '''brat''' (cloak).  }}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2006|title=Celtic Culture: A-Celti  |author= |page=1272 |ISBN=1851094407 |passage=Women wore loose, flowing, ankle-length robes modelled on 11th-century European fashion (derived from what O'Neill called the léine) and, perhaps, a '''brat''' over these. }}
# {{lb|en|obsolete|UK|Scotland|dialect}} A coarse kind of [[apron]] for keeping the clothes clean; a [[bib]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1882|author=John Strathesk|title=Blinkbonny|chapter=pp. 135|edition=|url=[http://books.google.com/books?id=ga0yAQAAMAAJ&pg=PA382 The English Dialect Dictionary... ''brat'']|passage=[She] had still on the rough worsted apron of nappy homespun wool, called a '''"brat"'''.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} The [[young]] of an [[animal]].
#* {{RQ:Marlowe Tamburlaine|part=1|scene=iii|page=51|passage=Their ſhoulders broad, for complet armour fit,<br>Their lims more large and of a bigger ſize<br>Than all the '''brats''' yſprong from ''Typhons'' loins:}}
#* {{quote-text|en|year=1680|author=w:Roger L'Estrange|title=Citt and Bumpkin
|passage=They are your Will-Worship-men, your Prelates '''Brats''': Take the whole Litter of’um, and you’ll finde never a barrel better Herring.}}

==Vestinian==

===Etymology===
{{etymon|xvs|:inh|itc-pro:*gʷrāt(i)s}}
From {{inh|xvs|itc-pro|*gʷrāt(i)s}}, from {{der|xvs|ine-pro|*gʷerH-}}.

===Noun===
{{head|xvs|noun}}<ref>{{R:itc:EDL|page=271|head=grātus}}</ref><ref>{{R:itc-sbl:The Italic Dialects|vol=II|page=605}}</ref><ref>{{R:itc-sbl:Wallace:1984|pages=75-76}}</ref>

# [[grace]], [[mercy]]
#* {{RQ:xvs:CILI394}}

====Usage notes====
* The phrase this term appears within is itself a common phrase throughout Sabellic languages. Compare "{{l|xvs||brat data}}" to "{{cog|osc||brateis datas}}" or "{{cog|pgn||brais datas}}." In these phrases, the form equivalent to {{l|xvs|brat}} is an abbreviation.
* De Vaan categorizes the term as a genitive singular but Conway categorizes it as an ablative feminine singular in an ablative absolute construction.
* The inscription this term was found in likely represents a dialect formed from a mix of Latin and Vestinian features
